diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

quality.label: Quality according to the media server

diagnostics.ordered: Media goes through a relay over TCP/TLS. This path doesn't drop packets — it re-requests them, and everything that arrives after waits for the late one. To the ear it sounds like “went quiet, then talked faster”. The buffer has been raised automatically. If this keeps happening, check that your network lets UDP through to the media server: the direct path is noticeably smoother.
diagnostics.videoPaused_one: Video was paused for you {{count}} time: your connection couldn't keep up with the picture, so the server kept speech and music going. The picture comes back on its own when the connection improves.
diagnostics.videoPaused_other: Video was paused for you {{count}} times: your connection couldn't keep up with the picture, so the server kept speech and music going. The picture comes back on its own when the connection improves.
diagnostics.footnote: This check measures the app server's response time. The audio and video route, packet loss, and RTT to the media server appear below once tracks are flowing in the meeting.
diagnostics.noTracks: There are no active tracks in the meeting yet. The local device check doesn't send a test to the media server.

stuck.title: Picture or sound frozen?

warning.title: Windows will show a warning
warning.text: The installer isn't signed with a publisher certificate, so SmartScreen will say “Windows protected your PC” and call the publisher unknown. It says this about any new program without a paid certificate, not about this one in particular.
warning.details: In the warning window, click More info.
warning.after: This happens once, during installation. After that Cord starts normally: the “downloaded from the internet” mark is on the downloaded file, not on what the installer puts on disk. With the portable version, the mark stays on the unpacked files, so the installer is the smoother option.

support.title: Support
support.lead: Answers to common questions, a camera and microphone check, and a way to reach us.

camera.q: The camera won’t turn on or shows a black screen
camera.a:
Allow camera access: the camera icon in the address bar → “Allow”, then reload the page.
Close apps that hold the camera: Zoom, Teams, OBS or another tab with a meeting.
In “Settings → Video”, pick the right camera — a laptop with an external camera has two.
In the Windows app, check “Settings → Privacy → Camera”: camera access for apps must be on.

microphone.a:
Look at the microphone button at the bottom: crossed out means the microphone is off.
In “Settings → Microphone”, pick a microphone and say something — the level bar should move.
The browser may have blocked access: the icon in the address bar → “Allow”.
On a quiet microphone, strict noise suppression cuts speech — try another option in the same settings.

silent.a:
If the stage shows a “Turn on meeting sound” button, click it: the browser plays no sound until the first click on the page.
Check “Settings and actions” — the sound of the whole meeting may be turned off.
One person’s volume is in the right-click menu on them; the overall volume is in “Settings → Microphone → Speakers”.
There, also pick your headphones or speakers and run the test.

screen.a:
Click the screen button at the bottom and pick a window, a tab or the entire screen.
On macOS, allow screen recording: “System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording”, then restart the browser.
For others to hear the sound, share a tab or the entire screen and tick the audio option in the picker.
Phone browsers can’t always share the screen — a computer works better.

smartscreen.a:
This is the SmartScreen warning: Cord doesn’t have a paid publisher certificate yet, and Windows says this about any new program.
Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. You only need to do this once, during installation.

network.q: The connection drops, video looks blocky
network.a:
Pause downloads and streams on the same connection; a cable or Wi‑Fi close to the router is noticeably steadier.
VPNs and corporate networks sometimes get in the way of a direct connection — without them, sound and video lag less.
In the meeting, open “Settings and actions → Diagnostics”: it shows the path, loss and delay — you can attach them to your request.
